## Critique
- claim-1: Within the stated regime \(\min(i,j)=2\) and \(\min(q-i,r-j)=1\), the partition enumeration and Pieri expansions are correct and establish the requested local completeness. The boundary conditions for \(u\) and \(w\) are also correct. One defect remains in the determinant witness: when \((p,c)=(1,1)\), the complementary array on columns \((z,y_2)\) is \(3\times2\), so its determinant is undefined without specifying two selected rows. Moreover, after truncation rows (2) and (4) coincide in this case. Thus the claimed determinant \(-1\) needs an explicit row selection. The argument proves only this parameter regime; that scope must be identified as the intended certificate scope.

## Required revisions
- For \((p,c)=(1,1)\), display the boundary matrix
  \[
  \begin{pmatrix}
  0&1&1\\
  1&1&0\\
  0&1&1
  \end{pmatrix}_{(x_2,z,y_2)}
  \]
  and specify that rows (2),(3) on columns \((z,y_2)\) give
  \[
  \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
  \qquad \det=-1.
  \]
  State explicitly that rows (2) and (4) are equal here.
- Clarify that “complete row list” is an indexed list of Pieri products, so coincident boundary rows are retained as distinct indexed rows.
- State explicitly that the certificate is established only under \(\min(i,j)=2\) and \(\min(q-i,r-j)=1\). No broader completeness claim follows.
